title: DebianSourcePreparationV1
description:
The full `DebianSourcePreparationV1` report.

The runtime binds this to the Evidence row as a `Report` artifact (PHASE-1.md §31, 1A.3). The `evidence.artifact.read` MCP tool (1A.4) reads it back.

candidate_fingerprint.description: The candidate the tool was invoked against. Echoed back so the Evidence row is self-describing without a join.

diagnostics.description: Per-check failure / informational lines. Empty when `verdict` is `pass`.

findings.description: Per-check results. Populated even when the verdict is `fail`; the agent can see *which* check failed.

identity.description: The first-entry identity from `debian/changelog`. `None` when `changelog_parsable` is `false`.

report_kind.description: Always `debian.source_preparation`. Discriminates this report from `debian.source_analysis_v1` (1C.2) and `debian.maintenance_context_v1` (1C.3). Stored as `String` rather than `&'static str` so the deserialised struct can be a normal owned value (a `&'static str` field forces the deserialiser to require `'static` lifetime on its input).

schema_version.description: Always `1` for this revision. Bump on incompatible wire-format changes.

Diagnostic.description: A single failure or informational line from the tool.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `E_DEBIAN_DIR_MISSING`. Future tools can match on this without parsing the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. The tool does not embed the offending value (a) to keep PII out of the report and (b) so the same diagnostic text can serve any fixture.

path.description: The on-disk path that triggered the diagnostic, when applicable (e.g. `debian/`, `debian/changelog`).

SourcePreparationFindings.description: Per-check results. The fields are populated whether the tool's `verdict` is `pass`, `fail`, or `infrastructure_error`; the agent (or the next normalizer down the line) can use them to decide what to do. A `false` flag here is *not* a re-statement of the verdict — the verdict aggregates the flags plus any cross-checks (e.g. a `Fail` is set even when all flags are `true` if the changelog says version `1.0.0-1` but the candidate says `1.0.0`).

changelog_source_name.description: Source name parsed from `debian/changelog` (the first-entry's name field). The value is always present when `changelog_parsable` is `true`.

changelog_version.description: Version parsed from `debian/changelog` (the first-entry's version field). The value is always present when `changelog_parsable` is `true`.

control_source_name.description: Source name parsed from `debian/control`. The value is always present when `control_parsable` is `true`; `None` otherwise.

control_source_name_matches_candidate.description: Whether the control-parsed source name matches the candidate's `source_name`.

rules_executable.description: `debian/rules` exists and is executable. Read but not enforced for the 1C.1 verdict (a non-executable rules is a build-time concern, not a source-preparation one).

oneOf.description: At least one §17 check failed (mismatched name, mismatched version, unparsable `debian/control`, unparsable `debian/changelog`, missing `debian/`, unidentifiable source format, unparsable mandatory metadata). Diagnostics list the specific failure.

The tool could not establish the fact at all: the workspace path is unreadable, an IO error occurred, a parser binary is missing. The §17 rule "parser binary missing → InfrastructureError" lives here.
